subject: Vectorly MSA + Order Form — intake: template synthesis & risk flags
messages:
From: Sarah Tran <sarah@vectorly.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Vectorly MSA + Order Form — intake and early asks

Hi team,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — we’re excited to move forward. Attached are the initial MSA (draft) and a simple order form with anticipated seat counts and an implementation milestone schedule. Two quick flags from our side:

- Data residency: some data will be stored in our US-East cloud tenant, but we may require EU-hosted backups for EU users (likely later in the year).
- Security: we have a standard vendor questionnaire and we’ll need SOC 2 evidence and an encryption at rest confirmation.

Can you confirm: 1) which of your commercial templates would be applied (Redwood standard MSA vs. marketplace template), 2) rough timeline for a first-pass redline, and 3) point person for procurement/billing?

Attaching: Vectorly_Draft_MSA_v1.docx; OrderForm_Initial.xlsx; Vectorly-Security-Appendix.pdf

Best,
Sarah Tran
VP, Business Operations
Vectorly

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Tran <sarah@vectorly.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 10:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Vectorly MSA + Order Form — intake and early asks

Sarah — thanks for sending and for the clear flags. Quick triage below; will follow up with formal redline plan by EOD Monday.

Triage / answers to your questions:
1) Template: we typically propose Redwood Standard MSA v2026-11 for new commercial relationships; if Vectorly requires a marketplace flow we can map differences, but standard MSA is the starting point.
2) Timeline: first-pass legal redline (internal) — 5 business days; external redline to Vectorly — ~7 business days after that, assuming limited negotiation. If you need an accelerated path, mention preferred cutoff dates and we can prioritize.
3) Procurement/Billing point: looping in Marissa (Contracts & Onboarding) for billing contacts and invoice cadence.

Primary risks to flag now:
- Data residency conditionality (EU backup = potential exhibit requirement).
- Liability caps and indemnity carveouts in your draft (will need clause-by-clause review).
- Hosting/residency references that might trigger an augmented security review — please confirm which product modules will see EU user data.

Action items (internal):
- Marissa: own billing/pricing and signer map.
- Karthik: lead redline on commercial terms + jurisdiction/authority pockets.
- I’ll coordinate SOC 2 evidence intake and propose template mapping.

I’ll attach our Redwood Standard MSA and a short variant table in the Monday note.

Thanks — kim

--
Kimberly Park
Head of Contracts & Risk Operations
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Vectorly MSA + Order Form — intake and early asks

Sarah / team — I have the billing/contact stub request. For Vectorly’s order form: can you confirm the billing cadence (monthly vs quarterly) and primary payer email for PO routing? I’ll assemble the signer matrix and expected approver windows (should help speed signoff).

I’ll also validate seat counts against our pricing grid and flag any discount tiers if you’re over 2,500 seats.

Quick note to Kimberly & Karthik: I’ll prepare the signer map and invoice flow doc by Wednesday.

Thanks — m

--
Marissa Cole
Senior Manager, Customer Onboarding & Billing
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Sarah Tran <sarah@vectorly.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Vectorly MSA + Order Form — intake and early asks

Thanks — quick follow from legal redline perspective.

Notes / asks:
- Template variant: if Vectorly expects an EU backup exhibit, we’ll need to create Exhibit D for residency and a separate data processing addendum (DPA) that references EU subprocessors. That adds ~3 business days to the external redline cycle.
- Jurisdiction: Vectorly draft proposes Delaware courts; we generally prefer California or arbitration. If they push for Delaware, we’ll propose arbitration as fallback in the external round.
- Cap math: your draft has a per-claim cap that is higher than our standard 12-month revenue cap. I’ll propose language to preserve commercial flexibility while offering a modest increase for enterprise customers.
- Security evidence: can the Vectorly security appendix include a link to the SOC 2 report or redacted AOC? If so, send the link and I’ll route to InfoSec for verification.

Planned deliverable: I’ll upload an internal redline (tracked changes) to the shared Drive folder by EOB today. External redline to Vectorly targeted for Wed next week, assuming SOC 2 evidence is available.

Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference
